title: The Grove Liquidity Layer segregates capital into two Allocator Vaults, one for general ALM and one for the Diamond PAU
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.1.1.1.1 gives the Liquidity Layer's capital structure in three sentences: "The Grove Liquidity Layer operates two Allocator Vaults, each with an associated Allocator Buffer. The ALLOCATOR-BLOOM-A Allocator Vault and Buffer serve the monolithic ALM Controller for general allocation activity. The ALLOCATOR-GROVE-A Allocator Vault and Buffer serve the Diamond PAU."

The **vault/buffer pairing** is the primitive unit. A vault holds the position; a buffer holds working balance against it, so allocation activity does not require touching the vault on every operation. Pairing them one-to-one means a buffer is never shared across strategies, and a drain on one cannot starve the other.

The **two-vault split** is a strategy-level firewall. General allocation runs through a single "monolithic ALM Controller" against BLOOM-A; the Diamond PAU — which surfaces elsewhere as its own Uniswap Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.1.2.1.12.3, "Grove Diamond PAU Uniswap v3 AUSD/USDC") — runs against GROVE-A. A specialized, presumably more active strategy is therefore capitalized separately from the main book, so its failure mode is bounded by its own vault's balance.

Calling the general controller "monolithic" is a candid architectural admission: one controller mediates all general allocation activity across every protocol and chain listed in the Instance directory. That is a single point of both control and failure, and it is the counterpart to the per-Instance granularity of the governance layer — many governed positions, one execution path.
description: ALLOCATOR-BLOOM-A serves the monolithic ALM Controller while ALLOCATOR-GROVE-A serves the Diamond PAU; each vault is paired with its own Allocator Buffer.
